reason: When the Hebrew people cry out to Moses in distress, directly accusing him ('Why hast thou dealt thus with us, to carry us out of Egypt?'), Moses does not accept accountability or responsibility for their situation. Instead of acknowledging fault or addressing their concerns directly, he deflects to divine intervention, telling them 'Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord... The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.' The text shows no attempt by Moses to take responsibility for the state of the people or to address their legitimate grievances about the dire circumstances, only exhortations to trust God while remaining passive.
